subject: Large differences in RMSEA value in multigroup analysis - Lavaan versus mimic EQS

messages.author: 25a6c6f4afee9ffa
messages.subject: Large differences in RMSEA value in multigroup analysis - Lavaan versus mimic EQS
parts:
Dear all,
 
I am running some multigroup CFA and SEM analyses with Lavaan "as such", Lavaan mimicking EQS, and Lavaan mimicking Mplus.
 
Not surprisingly, the fit values that the three options yield are pretty similar, except for the RMSEA. Each time the Lavaan "as such" and the "mimic Mplus" options give an RMSEA that is about three times as large as the one that the "mimic EQS" option gives (e.g., 0.036 versus 0.012). It seems to me that something went wrong. I would be very grateful if someone could explain the large difference in RMSEA to me, and tell me which version I can best adhere to. One thing that might be relevant is that the number of groups is equal to nine (three^2) in my analyses.
 
Kind regards,
Ivo van der Lans

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Large differences in RMSEA value in multigroup analysis - Lavaan versus mimic EQS
parts:
On 01/17/2014 01:23 PM, ivo.van...@wur.nl wrote:
> Dear all,
> I am running some multigroup CFA and SEM analyses with Lavaan "as such",
> Lavaan mimicking EQS, and Lavaan mimicking Mplus.
> Not surprisingly, the fit values that the three options yield are pretty
> similar, except for the RMSEA. Each time the Lavaan "as such" and the
> "mimic Mplus" options give an RMSEA that is about three times as
> large as the one that the "mimic EQS" option gives (e.g., 0.036 versus
> 0.012). It seems to me that something went wrong.

From the source (lav_fit_measures.R), and slightly simplifying:

if(object@Options$mimic %in% c("Mplus", "lavaan")) {
RMSEA <- sqrt( max( c((X2/N)/df - 1/N, 0) ) ) * sqrt(G)
} else {
RMSEA <- sqrt( max( c((X2/N)/df - 1/N, 0) ) )
}

So both lavaan and Mplus multiply by sqrt(G) (G is the number of
groups), while EQS does not do so. When in doubt, I would trust lavaan ;-)

The formula for multiple group setting is given by Steiger:

Steiger, JH (1998). A note on multiple sample extensions of the RMSEA
fit index. Structural Equation Modling, 5(4), 411-419..

Yves.
